gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each additional kWh costs when you expand these home-backup systems: EcoFlow's DELTA Pro Ultra-series battery is $382/kWh, BLUETTI's B300K is $397/kWh and Jackery's Battery Pack 3600 Plus is $404/kWh, while Anker's BP3800 is $521/kWh and Jackery's Battery Pack 5000 Plus is $516/kWh.
standout_why: StormWatts (cited) works out $/kWh only for the base units: Jackery HomePower 3600 Plus about $530, Anker F3800 Plus about $677, EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 about $683. It has no expansion-battery prices, no solar refill hours and no Wh/lb. EnergySage (cited) lists price, Wh, solar input and weight but works out none of these figures. I could not open SolarGenReview (HTTP 429) or TheOutagePlan (certificate error), so I could not check whether they have these figures.
decides: For a shopper who will grow past about 4 kWh, the add-on battery price matters more than the base price. Anker's F3800 Plus has the most solar input of the units checked here (3,200 W), but every Anker kWh you add costs about 30% more than Jackery's 3600-series pack or BLUETTI's B300K ($521 vs $404 or $397). Jackery HomePower 3600 Plus with 2 packs gives 10.75 kWh for $4,797 ($446/kWh). BLUETTI Apex 300 with 2× B300K gives 8.29 kWh for $3,689 ($445/kWh). Both cost far less per kWh than Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus with 1 pack ($605/kWh) or the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X 12 kWh bundle ($643/kWh). This backs a 'best value for expandable home backup' pick of the HomePower 3600 Plus or the Apex 300 over ChatGPT's DELTA Pro Ultra. It also shows that our page's $1,349 for Jackery's Battery Pack 3600 is out of date.

findings.label: Ideal solar refill time at maximum solar input
findings.value: 1.26 h base; 7.6 h with 5 packs (30.24 kWh)
findings.note: 5,040 Wh ÷ 4,000 W = 1.26 h; 30,240 Wh ÷ 4,000 W = 7.6 h. Ignores charging losses and weather. Jackery's own page says 'about 2 hours' for the base unit.
